results.title: Health AI in 2026: CU Researchers are Implementing Trustworthy ...
results.content: ## University of Colorado researchers are building Large Language Models (LLMs) that enhance clinical decision making while prioritizing safety, transparency and trust. Researchers in the Department of Biomedical Informatics (DBMI) at the University of Colorado Anschutz (CU Anschutz) are leveraging LLMs to improve healthcare—seeking to improve the experience of both patients and clinicians. However, this introduction of LLMs into healthcare raises a poignant question: can we trust these AIs to support clinicians and patients? “We want to assure that when LLMs present a predicted diagnosis, they can accurately convey *why*they made this prediction and *how confident they are* in their prediction,” said Gao. This process of quantifying confidence of predictions is a form of uncertainty estimation (or uncertainty quantification), and it is part of what Gao and the LARK Lab are researching. Tools like MUSE will support the use of LLMs in diagnostic decision making by helping clinicians to understand the confidence of an LLM’s prediction.

results.title: Reliability of Large Language Model Generated Clinical Reasoning ...
results.content: Methods: In a blinded comparative study at a clinical center, senior clinicians in assisted reproductive technology evaluated CoTs generated via 3 distinct strategies: zero-shot, random few-shot (using random shallow examples), and selective few-shot (using diverse, high-quality examples). We hypothesize that a selective few-shot strategy, meticulously crafted with diverse and deeply reasoned examples, will improve the factual accuracy, logical clarity, and clinical information use of LLM-generated reasoning in infertility decision-making scenarios, compared with generic zero-shot and random few-shot prompting. Through systematic comparisons, we show that a selective few-shot prompting strategy, which is based on the “dual principles” of gold-standard depth and representative diversity, substantially improves the quality and reliability of generated ART CoTs. This offers a feasible, cost-effective blueprint for generating trustworthy ART synthetic data at scale, without requiring immense annotated datasets. Finally, this study evaluates the clinical reliability of LLM-generated reasoning in the ART context as a step toward addressing data scarcity in explainable, domain-specialized AI development.

[by Melinda Lammert](https://news.cuanschutz.edu/dbmi/author/melinda-lammert) | February 25, 2025. The [University of Colorado Anschutz Medical Campus](https://www.cuanschutz.edu/) (CU Anschutz) recently hosted its inaugural conference on AI, titled "Engaging with AI." This event provided a platform to explore how AI is transforming research, education, and collaboration across various disciplines. Casey Greene, PhD, founding chair of the [Department of Biomedical Informatics](https://medschool.cuanschutz.edu/dbmi) (DBMI), remarked, "At DBMI, we take great pride in being the academic foundation at CU Anschutz, pioneering initiatives that seamlessly integrate cutting-edge technology with an unwavering commitment to advancing clinical excellence.". During the event, [Yanjun Gao](https://som.cuanschutz.edu/Profiles/Faculty/Profile/39558), PhD, assistant professor of [biomedical informatics](https://medschool.cuanschutz.edu/dbmi) at the [University of Colorado School of Medicine](https://medschool.cuanschutz.edu/), presented groundbreaking research from the [Language, Reasoning, Knowledge (LARK) Lab](https://www.larknlp.com/). Gao explained, “We are assessing whether these methods can ensure that LLMs align with human values when generating and evaluating clinical text, especially in healthcare contexts,” she added, “While we don’t have all the answers yet, we are actively working on these critical questions.” You can learn more [here](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.18170).
